clue.text: Browsing using Microsoft product, wishing to take in a little money

parts.note: Windows is Microsoft's operating system

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so the word for wishing wraps round the money

parts.note: wishing means hoping
p is a penny, a small coin

explanation.surface: Someone surfing the web on their PC, hoping to earn a bit of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browsing' suggests surfing the web with the Microsoft product, but here it means looking in shop windows.
explanation.definitionFit: Window-shopping is looking at goods in shops with no intention of buying, which is idle browsing.

clue.text: Flew back to Arkansas property, where government is responsible for social security

definitions.text: where government is responsible for social security

indicators.note: going back means the word flew is read from its end to its start

parts.note: taken as written
AR is the US postal abbreviation for Arkansas
an estate is a landed property

explanation.surface: Someone flew back to their land in Arkansas, in a country with state-funded social security.
explanation.definitionFit: A welfare state is a system in which the government takes responsibility for citizens' benefits, pensions and health care.

clue.text: Wanderer taking French name now

parts.note: nom is the French word for name
AD, anno domini, is the era we live in now

explanation.surface: A traveller adopting a French name these days.
explanation.walkthrough: AD (anno domini) stands for the present era, so it can mean now.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad roams from place to place with no fixed home, which makes them a wanderer.

clue.text: Spectators finding Serb wandering between deliveries

indicators.note: something between lies inside, so the shuffled letters sit within the cricket word

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by one bowler

indicators.note: letters that wander stray from their places and settle in a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Onlookers spot a Serbian roaming about between parcels or bowls.
explanation.walkthrough: Deliveries suggests parcels, but in cricket a bowler delivers the ball, six to an over.
explanation.definitionFit: Observers watch events without taking part, just as spectators do.

clue.text: Mockery made of Sam's car

indicators.note: something made of these is fashioned out of them, so the letters are built into a new word

parts.note: the letters of both words, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: People laughing at Sam's vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcasm is cutting, ironic language used to deride, which is a form of mockery.

clue.text: Sat quietly inside after love's resisted

indicators.note: after means the built word follows the letter for love

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: the quiet letter is set inside the word for sat

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone sat silently, having been rebuffed by their beloved.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes inside POSED right after its first letter, giving PPOSED, which follows O.
explanation.definitionFit: To be opposed is to have resisted or stood against something.

clue.text: Inquiry into Public Relations award

parts.note: PR is the usual abbreviation
the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

explanation.surface: An investigation into how a PR agency handed out a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inquiry into' reads as one phrase, but 'into' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A probe is a thorough investigation, so it serves as a noun for an inquiry.

clue.text: Want to find oriental ship docked in north-eastern town

indicators.note: a ship docked in a town lies within it, so these letters sit inside the town word

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation
a large town is a city
E for east
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: A wish to see an eastern vessel moored in a north-eastern port.
explanation.walkthrough: Want here is a noun meaning need, not the verb to desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Want can mean need or lack, and a necessity is something one needs.

clue.text: Fifty-one doctors are members

parts.note: L is fifty and I is one in Roman numerals
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: Fifty-one medics belong to some association.
explanation.definitionFit: Members is an old word for parts of the body, especially arms and legs, which are limbs.

clue.text: Blame for breaking compass

indicators.note: breaking into something gets inside it, so the word for 'for' splits the range word

parts.note: compass can mean range or extent, which is reach
pro is Latin for for, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Someone is blamed for smashing a navigational instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass looks like the navigator's tool, but here it is the scope or reach of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproach someone is to rebuke them and hold them at fault, which is to blame them.

clue.text: Order I gave dentist is looked into

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so the letters are put in a fresh sequence

parts.note: the letters of the three words

explanation.surface: An instruction I passed to the dentist is being examined.
explanation.definitionFit: Investigated means examined carefully, the same as looked into.

clue.text: No radar? Unusual in the Pyrenees

definitions.note: a place described by its location

indicators.note: an unusual version is out of the ordinary, so the letters fall into an unexpected order

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: Remarking that it is odd to have no radar up in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description of where the answer lies rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a tiny principality high in the Pyrenees mountains between France and Spain.

clue.text: Set about attaching ends of tassels on hat

indicators.note: turned about means moved round, so the three letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of set rearranged

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its first and last letters only

parts.note: its first and last letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sets about sewing tassels on to a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stetson is a wide-brimmed cowboy hat, named after its American maker.

clue.text: Bird of prey decapitated hunting dog

indicators.note: cutting off the head removes the first letter of the dog's name

parts.note: a beagle is a small hound bred for hunting hares

explanation.surface: A raptor has beheaded a hound.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle is a large hunting bird with a hooked beak and strong talons, a classic raptor.

clue.text: Develop germ in a test environment

indicators.note: an environment is the surroundings, so the run of clue words surrounds what is wanted

parts.note: read straight through, ignoring the word breaks

explanation.surface: Growing a microbe in a laboratory setting.
explanation.walkthrough: The words look like a straightforward lab description, but the answer runs right through them, stopping two letters short of the end of 'test'.
explanation.definitionFit: To germinate is to begin to grow, as a seed sprouts, so it means develop.

clue.text: Update way siren works

parts.note: a mode is a way of doing something

indicators.note: works as a verb means kneads or processes, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Improve the way an alarm functions.
explanation.definitionFit: To modernise is to bring something up to date, which is to update it.

clue.text: Tops up battery, but makes one pay again

definitions.meaning: first meaning: restores the electrical charge in a cell
second meaning: bills someone a second time

explanation.surface: A service that refills your battery but then bills you twice.
explanation.definitionFit: To recharge is both to refill a battery with power and to impose a charge on someone once more.

clue.text: Entrance her somehow in backstreet embrace

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the letters from the street word

parts.note: St, street, written back to front

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters come out in an arrangement of their own

parts.note: taken as written
to embrace someone is to hold them

explanation.surface: A doorway where a couple hug in a back alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backstreet' reads as an alley, but it is to be split: back plus street, the street abbreviation turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A threshold is the sill or doorstep at the entrance to a building, so it stands for an entrance.

clue.text: Torch is used to find bird

indicators.note: used letters have been worked over and put to another purpose, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: Someone shines a flashlight to track down a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is the large flightless African bird, the biggest living bird species.

clue.text: Picture used to explain how I had raised a weight

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means lifted up, so the short form of I had is read from bottom to top

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
taken as written
a gram is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: An illustration showing how I managed to lift a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'I had' is turned upward; 'a' and 'weight' follow in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a simplified drawing showing how something works, so it is a picture that explains.

clue.text: Weep over heartless poet in tomb

indicators.note: with its heart gone the word loses its middle letters
in an across clue over means placed before, so weep comes first

parts.note: to weep is to cry
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mourners weeping for a poet lying in his grave.
explanation.definitionFit: A crypt is an underground vault beneath a church, used as a burial chamber or tomb.

clue.text: Dense little alien goes into dense little wood

parts.note: dense means thick
E.T. is the little alien of the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A small stupid extraterrestrial wanders into a small tangled copse.
explanation.walkthrough: Dense first means thick, then in the definition means closely packed; 'goes into' links rather than inserts.
explanation.definitionFit: A thicket is a small area of tightly packed shrubs and trees, a dense little wood.

clue.text: Tortured kin with iron weapon

indicators.note: tortured means twisted out of shape, so the letters are wrenched into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Relatives tormented with a metal blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A knife is a blade that can be used as a weapon for stabbing.

clue.text: Extraordinary how asparagus starter has a degree of piquancy

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: its first letter
an MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree
zing is lively zest or tang

explanation.surface: A diner marvels at the tangy kick of an asparagus starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' poses as a first course on the menu, but it picks the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazing means astonishing or remarkable, the same as extraordinary.

clue.text: Artie's becoming extremely angry

indicators.note: becoming means turning into something else, so the name changes into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Artie is turning furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate describes someone who is furious or highly incensed, so it means extremely angry.

clue.text: Normal witch's pet

definitions.meaning: first meaning: well known, ordinary, everyday
second meaning: the spirit animal, often a cat, that attends a witch

explanation.surface: A witch's pet is just an ordinary one.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for something commonplace and a noun for the demon creature that serves a witch.

clue.text: Join key platform

parts.note: G is a musical key
a raft is a flat floating platform

explanation.surface: Connecting an important stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To graft is to unite a shoot onto a plant or tissue onto a body, which is to join.

clue.text: The Spanish, caught in double bind, cunningly pasted the new town

indicators.note: something caught in a trap is held inside it, so the Spanish article sits within the binding

parts.note: to hem is to bind an edge of cloth; double it
el is Spanish for the

indicators.note: cunningly suggests artful contrivance, so the letters are craftily rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Spaniards trapped in a dilemma craftily glued together a new settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: EL sits between the two HEMs; HEMEL HEMPSTEAD is a town in Hertfordshire, north of London, built up as one of Britain's post-war new towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's New Towns were planned settlements after 1946, and Hemel Hempstead was designated one of the first.
